issues.legal_issue: Joint owners with independent titles may receive separate ceiling units rather than being treated as one person holding a single unit.
material_facts: The two co-owners were strangers to one another and held independent title to the land as tenants in common, each with a half interest.
issues.conclusion: The co-owners were entitled to two separate units under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: For determining ceiling units under Sections 2(i) and 4 of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, co-owners with independent titles are not treated as one person merely because they hold land jointly. The Court observed that the definition of “person” merits liberal construction, but that these co-owners did not fall within it as one person.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_assessment: A proceeding determines the ceiling units applicable to people who hold land.
predicates.independent_joint_titles: The co-owners acquired and hold their interests independently of one another.
predicates.co_owners_hold_as_tenants_in_common: The co-owners hold the land as tenants in common.

issues.definition: When a ceiling assessment concerns co-owners with independent titles who hold as tenants in common, they receive separate ceiling units.

issues.legal_issue: Land required to remain open under applicable building regulations may be excluded from vacant land even when no building had been constructed on the appointed day.
material_facts: Building regulations limited construction on the plot to one-third of its area, requiring the remainder to be kept vacant.
A building plan had been sanctioned, although no construction had been raised on the appointed day.
The land was in a green colony where the plots could not be subdivided, and housing for weaker sections was not permitted there.
issues.conclusion: The co-owners were entitled to exclude from vacant land the area required to remain open under the building regulations and sanctioned building plan, despite the absence of construction on the appointed day.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(q)(i) excludes land on which construction is not permissible under applicable building regulations, and the Court held that its application does not require a building to exist on the appointed day. The statutory scheme, including Section 29, contemplated regulation of construction. The exclusionary clauses in the definition of vacant land are to be construed liberally.

rule.if: urban_land_ceiling_assessment and construction_permitted_by_regulations and approved_building_plan_exists and regulations_require_open_land

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_assessment: A proceeding determines what land counts toward a person's vacant-land ceiling.
predicates.construction_permitted_by_regulations: The applicable regulations permit construction on the relevant land.
predicates.approved_building_plan_exists: The owner obtained approval for a building plan for the land.
predicates.regulations_require_open_land: The applicable regulations require part of the land to remain open and unbuilt.

issues.definition: In a vacant-land ceiling assessment, land required to remain open under applicable regulations is excluded when construction is permitted and an approved building plan exists, even if no building has yet been constructed.

issues.legal_issue: The area of a dwelling structure held elsewhere is not counted toward the vacant-land ceiling when its owner holds no appurtenant vacant land there.
material_facts: The co-owners each owned a flat in another city.
They held no vacant land appurtenant to those flats and were entitled to possess and own the structures alone.
The Act defined vacant land exhaustively and excluded specified categories of land.
issues.conclusion: The area of the flats was not to be taken into consideration when determining the ceiling limit.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(q) and 4(9) must be read together: Section 4(9) requires the person to hold vacant land as well as other land on which there is a dwelling unit, and that other land must be land other than vacant land. The definition in Section 2(q), which uses “means,” is exhaustive, and its exclusionary clauses are to be construed liberally. Because the Act is expropriatory, it is construed strictly. The Court relied on M/s D.L.F. Qutab Enclave Complex Educational Charitable Trust v. State of Haryana, Bhavnagar University v. Palitana Sugar Mill, Wyre Forest District Council v. Secretary of State for the Environment, Meera Gupta v. State of West Bengal, Atma Ram Aggarwal v. State of U.P., and Kunj Behari Lal v. District Judge, Gorakhpur. It preferred Meera Gupta to State of U.P. v. L.J. Johnson, while noting that the conflict between those decisions had not been resolved in Angoori Devi v. State of U.P.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_assessment: A proceeding determines the vacant-land ceiling applicable to a person.
predicates.dwelling_structure_held_elsewhere: The person owns or holds a dwelling structure apart from the land under assessment.
predicates.no_appurtenant_vacant_land_held: The person holds no vacant land appurtenant to that dwelling structure.

issues.definition: When a vacant-land ceiling assessment concerns a person who holds a dwelling structure elsewhere but no appurtenant vacant land there, the area of that structure is not counted toward the vacant-land ceiling.
